requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation has reachable code and a test.

**Command form and alias**
- `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` (`Author`) declares the syntax. It takes `subject`, `--config`, `--stdout`, `-v/--verbose`, and `--missing` and `--force`.
- `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`.
- `alias = "author-evidence"` keeps the alias.
- Tests: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` runs `author-evidence`. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` runs `author-evidence`, `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout`, and the mutual-exclusion errors.
- `--config` is exercised in several `authoring_cli.rs` tests, for example `false_is_a_completed_assessment`.

**Authoring one existing requirement or named example under refresh**
- `main` passes the subject to `author_evidence_with_options` in `src/authoring/mod.rs`.
- That function parses the subject with `AuthoringSubject::parse`, whose `Definition` variant is the single command-line subject.
- It skips current subjects through `batch::subject_is_current` before resolving any configuration, and it treats `--stdout` as `--force`.
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` rejects a subject that is not an existing requirement or named example.
- Tests: the unknown-subject test above, `authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` for the refresh behavior, and the `authoring_cli.rs` tests that author a requirement.

**Report of subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage path**
- `AuthoringOutcome` carries those fields. `configured_assessment` fills them.
- `main` prints `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"`, then `Evidence: <path>`, then `Usage: <path>`.
- Test: `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts the subject and backend prefix, the model, `Evidence:` ending in `evidence/{SUBJECT}.json` and resolving to the actual file, and `Usage:`.

**Evidence destination: file path by default, `stdout` under `--stdout`**
- `EvidenceOutput` selects the destination. `configured_assessment` writes the file or stdout. `main` prints the path when `evidence_path` is `Some` and `Evidence: stdout` when it is `None`.
- Tests: the default-path assertions above, and `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files`, which asserts `Evidence: stdout\n` in stderr.

**Stdout mode sends the completion report and diagnostics to stderr**
- In stdout mode `main` uses `eprintln!` for the summary, `Evidence: stdout`, and `Usage:`.
- It also uses `eprintln!` for the `{subject}: false` line and the verbose rationale. `print_coverage_warnings` writes only to stderr, and errors go to stderr when `main` returns `Err`.
- Test: `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` parses the whole stdout as JSON, so nothing else is on stdout. It checks the report, the false line, the FIXME marker, and the verbose rationale in stderr, across true, false, and FIXME judgments and with and without `--verbose`. `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose` in default mode.

**Unspecified behavior**
- The extra subject forms (`citations:`, `sites:`) and `--policy` are marked as implementing other requirements, so they are not unspecified.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
